units.source: Electron API
The Electron API is the bridge between Trilium's interface and Electron's main process, exposed as the global __TRILIUM_PH_0__ in the desktop application.

It is not part of the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ global of script notes, but frontend scripts running in the desktop application can call it directly. It is __TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the browser and in the standalone build, so guard calls with __TRILIUM_PH_2__.

The complete surface exposed to the renderer as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ via __TRILIUM_PH_1__. The renderer must access Electron-only functionality through this object — direct __TRILIUM_PH_2__ and __TRILIUM_PH_3__ are unavailable because __TRILIUM_PH_4__ is disabled and __TRILIUM_PH_5__ is enabled.
The runtime value lives in __TRILIUM_PH_0__; this interface is the contract both the preload script (__TRILIUM_PH_1__) and the client (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) share.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Security:__TRILIUM_PH_1__ the scheme is matched against the allowlist in __TRILIUM_PH_2__ (commons). Blocked schemes include __TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__, __TRILIUM_PH_5__, __TRILIUM_PH_6__, __TRILIUM_PH_7__, __TRILIUM_PH_8__, and __TRILIUM_PH_9__ — they cover Follina-class RCE primitives (__TRILIUM_PH_10__, __TRILIUM_PH_11__), NTLM credential theft, and Java loader vectors. __TRILIUM_PH_0__Security:__TRILIUM_PH_1__ the path is canonicalized and must resolve to either the Trilium data directory (or a descendant) or the Trilium tmp directory (or a descendant). Anything else — absolute paths elsewhere on disk, traversal attempts, UNC paths that don't normalize under those roots — is rejected. Null bytes, empty strings, and non-existent files are also rejected, and so is a file whose extension makes the OS run it as a program (__TRILIUM_PH_2__, __TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__, __TRILIUM_PH_5__, __TRILIUM_PH_6__, __TRILIUM_PH_7__, __TRILIUM_PH_8__, __TRILIUM_PH_9__, an extension in __TRILIUM_PH_10__, …): the file was written from a note, which chose its name and content.

Opens a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ URL with its default OS handler. Exists as a separate channel from __TRILIUM_PH_1__ because neither Electron API opens every target correctly on Windows: __TRILIUM_PH_2__ mishandles Unicode characters in __TRILIUM_PH_3__ URLs, while __TRILIUM_PH_4__ opens a directory with the Explorer-specific __TRILIUM_PH_5__ verb, bypassing the user's file manager. The main process picks between them per target.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Security:__TRILIUM_PH_1__ the URL must use the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ scheme and must have an empty hostname. UNC paths (__TRILIUM_PH_3__) are explicitly blocked because Windows would otherwise resolve them to __TRILIUM_PH_4__ and leak the user's NTLM hash via SMB authentication. Drive-letter-as-host malformations like __TRILIUM_PH_5__ are normalized to __TRILIUM_PH_6__ before parsing.

Note: unlike __TRILIUM_PH_0__, the resolved path is NOT confined to the Trilium data / tmp directories — this channel handles user-clicked __TRILIUM_PH_1__ links inside note content, which routinely reference arbitrary locations on disk (__TRILIUM_PH_2__ and similar). Equivalent to a browser following a __TRILIUM_PH_3__ link the user clicked. A target that would run as a program — an executable extension as refused by __TRILIUM_PH_4__, or outside Windows a file with an execute bit — opens only after the user confirms it in a native dialog that defaults to Cancel. One such dialog is shown at a time; a cancel resolves to an empty string.
Parameter
Description
__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__A __TRILIUM_PH_2__ URL with an empty hostname.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Returns__TRILIUM_PH_1__ __TRILIUM_PH_2__: An empty string on success, or an error message on failure.
Triggers a Chromium download for the given URL — the file is saved through the normal "Save As" flow instead of being opened in the renderer.

The scheme, hostname, and port must all match the running app's origin (__TRILIUM_PH_2__ for the dev server, or the custom __TRILIUM_PH_3__ protocol for packaged Electron). Cross-origin downloads, hostless URLs (__TRILIUM_PH_4__, __TRILIUM_PH_5__, __TRILIUM_PH_6__, plain __TRILIUM_PH_7__), and unparseable URLs are rejected. This stops a compromised renderer from pre-positioning a remote payload in the user's Downloads folder under a familiar name.

The backup passphrase, kept encrypted by the OS keyring in a file outside the database (the database is what ends up inside the backup, so a passphrase stored there would ride along inside the very container it protects).
Deliberately write-only: there is no way to read the passphrase back, so a frontend script cannot exfiltrate it. Only the main process ever sees the plaintext again, when it writes a backup.

Both changes are also gated on a native OS confirmation, which a script can request but cannot answer. Without that, a script could quietly swap in a passphrase of its own and every later backup would be encrypted to it.

Desktop-native import that reads the user's file __TRILIUM_PH_0__in place__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (bounded memory, no temp copy) — the whole point being multi-GB __TRILIUM_PH_2__ archives, though any importable file is accepted. The renderer never handles a filesystem path: __TRILIUM_PH_3__ runs the OS dialog in the main process and returns opaque capability tokens, which __TRILIUM_PH_4__ redeems. A script can't forge a token or pass a path, so it can never read an arbitrary file.

Prompts a native "open file" dialog (multi-select, any type) and returns single-use tokens for the chosen files.

Resolves files the user dropped onto a drop zone to capability tokens, so a drag-and-drop import takes the same in-place (streamed) path as the dialog. The __TRILIUM_PH_0__ is the unforgeable capability: the path is obtained via __TRILIUM_PH_1__, which yields a real path only for a genuinely user-supplied file and an empty string for anything a script constructed — so a script can't smuggle in an arbitrary path. Returns __TRILIUM_PH_2__ when no dropped file resolved (e.g. dragged from a browser, not the OS), so the caller falls back to the normal upload route.
Parameter

__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__The files of the drop event.
